exit.en_def: To go out or go away from a place or situation; to depart, to leave.

ascend.en_def: To move upward, to fly, to soar.
ascend.en_example: He ascended to heaven upon a cloud.

flee.en_example: The prisoner tried to flee, but was caught by the guards.

rise.en_def: To go up; to ascend; to climb.

tumble.en_def: To move or rush in a headlong or uncontrolled way.

climb.en_def: To ascend; rise; to go up.

roll.en_def: To leave or begin a journey.
roll.en_example: I want to get there early; let's roll.

slide.en_def: To pass along smoothly or unobservedly; to move gently onward without friction or hindrance.
slide.en_example: A ship or boat slides through the water.

desert.en_def: To leave one's duty or post, especially to leave a military or naval unit without permission.
desert.en_example: Anyone found deserting will be punished.

descend.en_def: To pass from a higher to a lower place; to move downwards; to come or go down in any way, for example by falling, flowing, walking, climbing etc.
descend.en_example: The rain descended, and the floods came.

plunge.en_def: To fall or rush headlong into some thing, action, state or condition.
plunge.en_example: to plunge into debt;   to plunge into controversy

glide.en_def: To pass with a glide, as the voice.

swing.en_example: The children laughed as they swung.

bounce.en_def: To leap or spring suddenly or unceremoniously; to bound.
bounce.en_example: She bounced happily into the room.

hike.en_def: To take a long walk for pleasure or exercise.
hike.en_example: Don't forget to bring the map when we go hiking tomorrow.

roam.en_def: To wander or travel freely and with no specific destination.

dodder.en_def: To shake or tremble as one moves, especially as of old age or childhood; to totter.

wander.en_def: To go somewhere indirectly or at varying speeds; to move in a curved path.

march.en_def: To go to war; to make military advances.

amble.en_def: To stroll or walk slowly and leisurely.

lollop.en_def: To walk or move with a bouncing or undulating motion and at an unhurried pace.

limp.en_example: The business limped through the recession

inch.en_def: (followed by a preposition) To advance very slowly, or by a small amount (in a particular direction).
inch.en_example: Fearful of falling, he inched along the window ledge.

lurch.en_def: To make such a sudden, unsteady movement.

lumber.en_def: To move clumsily and heavily; to move slowly.

mince.en_def: To walk with short steps; to walk in a prim, affected manner.

mosey.en_def: To go off quickly: to hurry up.

parade.en_def: To assemble (soldiers, sailors) for inspection, to receive orders, etc.

plod.en_def: To walk or move slowly and heavily or laboriously (+ on, through, over).

promenade.en_def: To walk for amusement, show, or exercise.

prowl.en_def: To idle; to go about aimlessly.
prowl.en_example: That dandy has nothing better to do than prowl around town all day in his pinstripe suit.

rove.en_def: To pierce or cleave with a weapon.

ramble.en_def: To walk for pleasure; to amble or saunter.

perambulate.en_def: To walk about, roam or stroll.

shuffle.en_def: To move in a slovenly, dragging manner; to drag or scrape the feet in walking or dancing.
shuffle.en_example: He shuffled out of the room.

sneak.en_def: To creep or go stealthily; to come or go while trying to avoid detection, as a person who does not wish to be seen.
sneak.en_example: He decided to sneak into the kitchen for a second cookie while his mom was on the phone.

toddle.en_def: To walk in a carefree manner.
toddle.en_example: There he was, just toddling along.

wade.en_def: To walk through water or something that impedes progress.

gallop.en_def: To ride at a galloping pace.

rush.en_def: To flow or move forward rapidly or noisily.
rush.en_example: armies rush to battle;   waters rush down a precipice.

nip.en_def: To make a quick, short journey or errand, usually a round trip.
nip.en_example: Why don’t you nip down to the grocer’s for some milk?

scud.en_def: To run, or be driven, before a high wind with no sails set.

hurry.en_def: To hasten; to impel to greater speed; to urge on.

jog.en_def: (exercise) To move at a pace between walking and running, to run at a leisurely pace.

scurry.en_def: To run with quick light steps, to scamper.

speed.en_def: To cause to make haste; to dispatch with celerity; to drive at full speed; hence, to hasten; to hurry.

sprint.en_def: To run, cycle, etc. at top speed for a short period,

skedaddle.en_def: To move or run away quickly.

scram.en_def: Leave in a hurry, go away.
scram.en_example: What are you kids doing on my lawn? Scram!

tear.en_def: To move or act with great speed, energy, or violence.
tear.en_example: He tore into the backlog of complaints.

trot.en_def: To cause to move, as a horse or other animal, in the pace called a trot; to cause to run without galloping or cantering.

sweep.en_def: To move something in a long sweeping motion, as a broom.

cavort.en_def: To move about carelessly, playfully or boisterously.

jump.en_def: To flee; to make one's escape.

skip.en_example: The girls were skipping in the playground.

somersault.en_example: The performer somersaulted all the way across the stage.

romp.en_example: England romped to an easy win over Australia.

leap.en_def: To pass over by a leap or jump.
leap.en_example: to leap a wall or a ditch

whiz.en_def: To rush or move swiftly with such a sound.

creep.en_def: To have a sensation as of insects creeping on the skin of the body; to crawl.

clamber.en_def: To climb (something) with some difficulty, or in a haphazard fashion.
clamber.en_example: The children clambered over the jungle gym.

travel.en_def: To move illegally by walking or running without dribbling the ball.

ride.en_def: To be transported in a vehicle; to travel as a passenger.

backpack.en_def: To engage in low-cost, generally urban, travel with minimal luggage and frugal accommodations

sail.en_def: To ride in a boat, especially a sailboat.

accompany.en_def: To go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with.
accompany.en_example: Geoffrey accompanied the group on their pilgrimage.
